You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hot-Topic Strike｜2026.10.01 Main line: AI memory and rack-scale deployment｜Micron earnings · Rubin production · AMD Helios · custom chips

TEXT:
1. Micron blows out earnings; memory remains the AI bottleneck
On September 30, Micron reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $54.23 billion and adjusted EPS of $33.42, both above estimates. Fiscal Q1 revenue guidance is $61.5 billion ± $1.5 billion, with adjusted EPS of $38.15 ± $1. Commitments under long-term supply agreements rose to $32 billion from $22 billion in June, and remaining performance obligations are about $150 billion. The company said most of its fiscal 2027 HBM output is already locked in, and it raised capital spending. The stock rose less than 1% after hours.
🎯 Beneficiaries: MU , LRCX , AMAT ; key catalyst: the memory shortage narrative is confirmed by earnings, leaving a follow-through window for equipment and HBM names.
2. Vera Rubin NVL72 enters production workloads
CoreWeave said NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 is in limited availability on its cloud, with Cognition (Devin) the first customer running production workloads. Cognition measured up to 4.8x total token throughput versus GB200 NVL72 on software-engineering inference. CoreWeave said AI agent sandbox startup on the Vera CPU is more than 3x faster. NVIDIA closed up 0.51%.
🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA , CRWV ; key catalyst: Rubin has moved from launch to customer production; watch cloud rollout pace and inference orders.
3. HPE wins a $1.2 billion AMD Helios order
HPE received a $1.2 billion order from cloud firm Vultr to deploy AMD Helios racks, its first order for the system. Each rack carries 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs, paired with EPYC Venice CPUs, Pensando NICs, and HPE Juniper switches. Networking revenue CAGR for fiscal 2026–2029 was raised to the high teens, and fiscal 2027 networking growth was raised to the high teens to low 20s. Shares rose about 4%–6% intraday. 🎯 Beneficiaries: HPE, AMD; key catalyst: AMD’s rack solution lands a cloud order, with the networking outlook raised at the same time.
4. Synopsys signs a $1 billion-plus chip IP deal with Amazon
Synopsys and AWS signed a multi-year silicon IP license worth more than $1 billion. Amazon is the lead customer for application-optimized IP, covering custom chips and cloud infrastructure. Synopsys will also adopt AWS compute, storage, and Bedrock. The companies did not specify whether the IP lands on Graviton or Trainium.
🎯 Beneficiaries: SNPS , AMZN ; key catalyst: cloud custom silicon extends from design tools to IP licensing, adding orders along the custom ASIC chain.
5. Apple ’s October 13 smart-home event, OpenAI DevDay lands the same week
Gurman said Apple plans to launch its first smart-home hub, codenamed J490, on October 13, along with a 2027 HomePod mini and a new Apple TV. Apple closed up 1.10%. OpenAI’s San Francisco developer conference released more than 20 updates, including personal agent Dots and the GPT -6.1 Sol model. Meta closed down 1.84%. 🎯 Beneficiaries: AAPL , META; key catalyst: the on-device home hardware window is near, and the personal-agent narrative is entering a product comparison phase.
6. BofA raises the AI infrastructure market; Intel outperforms
BofA lifted its 2026–2030 AI data-center systems addressable market to $2.2 trillion from $1.8 trillion, and the annual pace to 40% from 33%. Near-term top picks include NVDA, INTC , MU, MRVL (Analyst Day on October 6), and LRCX. Intel closed up 3.71%. On the macro side, cooler-than-expected inflation cut October hike odds to about 37%. The S&P 500 fell 0.25%, the Nasdaq rose 0.24%, and the Dow fell 0.86%. 🎯 Beneficiaries: INTC, MRVL, NVDA; key catalyst: a sell-side upgrade plus Intel fund inflows, with MRVL’s Analyst Day imminent.
Trading note: Flows are still tracking memory earnings, Rubin production, and the AMD rack order. Custom chips and the Apple home chain are the event-driven side trades. With rates still elevated and indexes split, prioritize volume and guidance confirmation, and do not extrapolate a single day’s move.
US stocks have been more volatile recently. The above is for information only and is not investment advice.
